novel_features.name: Decay detector
novel_features.description: Flag underperforming videos by views-per-day vs the channel baseline (--metric velocity, default), with a --days window and a noise warning at <30 videos.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local join across the cached videos table — no single Data v3 endpoint returns this. Velocity normalization (views/day) prevents false positives where older videos look like outliers purely because they had more time to accumulate views.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Tells the creator which videos to re-promote or re-edit, before the algorithm forgets them.

novel_features.name: Retention leaderboard
novel_features.description: Top videos by average view percentage from Analytics API. Statistically noisy with <30 videos in the lookback window — treat as directional.
novel_features.rationale: Needs Analytics API + a sort the web UI does not expose per-video.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Ranks content by attention, not just views — the actual retention signal.

novel_features.name: Subscriber velocity
novel_features.description: Daily subscriber gain/loss rate from Analytics, day-bucketed.
novel_features.rationale: Needs OAuth Analytics API; the public Data v3 only reports rolling totals.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pinpoints which days a creator added or lost subs so launch-day pulls become visible.

novel_features.name: Competitor diff
novel_features.description: Compare uploads/cadence/avg views across cached channels (your channel + competitors).
novel_features.rationale: Requires N channels in one SQLite store; nothing public ranks them side-by-side.
novel_features.why_it_matters: One call answers 'how does my niche move?' without leaving the terminal.

novel_features.name: Posting cadence
novel_features.description: Correlate publish day-of-week or hour-of-day with average views.
novel_features.rationale: Needs all of a channel's videos plus their stats in one table — only possible with the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces the channel's actual best posting window from observed data, not folklore.

novel_features.name: CTR cohort
novel_features.description: Impressions and click-through-rate per video (Analytics API).
novel_features.rationale: Card impressions/CTR are only in Analytics, not public Data v3.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Tells the creator which thumbnails earn the click before they reroll the entire batch.

novel_features.name: Transcript search
novel_features.description: Full-text search across scraped transcripts (offline, FTS5).
novel_features.rationale: No public API returns video transcripts in bulk — this scrapes timedtext, persists locally, then queries via SQLite FTS5.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent grep an entire channel's spoken content offline, with no quota cost.

novel_features.name: Theme miner
novel_features.description: Extract most-repeated bigrams/trigrams from cached comments (FAQ surface area).
novel_features.rationale: Needs every comment in one place — Data v3 returns them paginated per video.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Shows what audience actually talks about so the creator picks topics with proven demand.

novel_features.name: Comment FAQ
novel_features.description: Surface most-liked question-shaped comments across cached videos.
novel_features.rationale: The web UI buries questions in noise; with everything in SQLite we just rank by likes + question-shape.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Generates a ready-to-answer Q&A pipeline straight from the audience.

novel_features.name: Topic cluster
novel_features.description: Group videos into topic clusters by tag overlap and rank by avg views.
novel_features.rationale: Needs every video + tags in one table; no API endpoint clusters videos topically.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reveals which themes pull views, not just which individual videos won.

novel_features.name: Quota-aware sync plan
novel_features.description: Estimate Data v3 quota units needed for a full refresh + comment sync, with daily-quota headroom.
novel_features.rationale: Calculated from what's already in the local store — no external tool knows your channel's video count locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prevents the surprise 'quotaExceeded' that wipes a creator's tooling for the day.

narrative.headline: The terminal-native YouTube CLI that unifies Data, Analytics, and transcripts in one offline SQLite store — so agents can compound queries without burning your 10K daily quota.
narrative.value_prop: youtube-pp-cli wraps both the YouTube Data API v3 and the YouTube Analytics API v2 behind one binary, scrapes transcripts with no auth, and syncs everything to a local FTS5-indexed SQLite store. After one morning sync, decay detection, retention leaderboards, theme mining, and competitor diffs all run locally at zero quota cost — surfaces no web dashboard or MCP server ships today.
narrative.auth_narrative: Two auth surfaces coexist. `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` (a free key from Google Cloud Console) unlocks public Data v3 reads — channel and video metadata, comments, captions list, transcript scraping. OAuth2 (installed-app flow with refresh token cached at `~/.config/youtube-pp-cli/token.json`) unlocks YouTube Analytics v2 and owner-only Data v3 fields. Run `youtube-pp-cli auth login` once; the CLI opens a browser, captures the consent code on localhost, and stores the refresh token. `auth status` shows scope coverage; `auth logout` clears it.

quickstart.comment: Confirms config path, auth source, and API reachability before anything else.
Reports whether the OAuth refresh token is cached (run `auth login` first if missing).
Quota-aware estimate of how many Data v3 units a full refresh would cost — run before any heavy sync.
Surfaces cached videos whose views fell 30%+ below the channel's rolling baseline.
Top videos by average view percentage straight from Analytics API.

troubleshoots.symptom: `quotaExceeded` error from any Data v3 command
troubleshoots.fix: 10K units/day is per-project. Wait for midnight Pacific Time reset, or create a second Google Cloud project and rotate `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`. Avoid `search list` (100 units/call) — prefer `videos list --id` (1 unit) and the offline `search` command after `sync`.

troubleshoots.symptom: `invalid_grant` or `Token has been expired or revoked` on OAuth calls
troubleshoots.fix: Refresh tokens expire after 6 months of disuse or when the user changes their Google password. Run `youtube-pp-cli auth login` again to re-grant.

troubleshoots.symptom: `transcripts get` returns empty or `no transcripts available`
troubleshoots.fix: The video may have transcripts disabled, be age-restricted, region-blocked, or auto-captioning not yet processed. Try `--lang en-US,en` or fall back to `--via yt-dlp` (requires yt-dlp installed).
The OAuth scope `yt-analytics.readonly` is required. Run `youtube-pp-cli auth status` to confirm; if missing, `auth logout` then `auth login` again and accept all consent prompts.

troubleshoots.symptom: `sync` is slow or hits quota on a large channel
troubleshoots.fix: Run `youtube-pp-cli sync plan --videos --comments --analytics` first to see the unit estimate, then sync incrementally with `--since <date>` or `--limit N`.

narrative.when_to_use: Use youtube-pp-cli when you want to answer real questions about a YouTube channel from the terminal or from an agent: 'which videos are decaying?', 'what do my comments keep asking?', 'how does my upload cadence compare to my competitors?'. It's the right tool when one-off API calls are not enough — when you want a local store that compounds, an FTS5 transcript index, and derived metrics that no dashboard ships. It is NOT the right tool for uploading videos (use YouTube Studio), live streaming, or downloading video files (use yt-dlp).
